svg.title: LMU with Sim-QVFR: everything in a frame
svg.text: LMU with Sim-QVFR: everything in a frame
Every step Sim-QVFR adds to a Le Mans Ultimate frame, in the order it runs. LMU runs its own two eye passes as shipped;
its code isn’t changed, hooked or called, and nothing is written into its memory. Details: the three diagrams named at the foot.

g.text: Sim-QVFR, loaded as an OpenXR API layer
No bytes changed, nothing hooked, no
VR eye loop: its own two passes
Final blit, driver tags, VR UI
Render scale, recommended size, FSR on
Another build: from OpenXR and the draws
FOV crop, gaze, focus boxes, jitter
On Microsoft’s d3d11.dll objects, not LMU’s
Gets an ordinary stereo frame, or on
Pimax and Varjo the four views as quad
Sim-QVFR’s own, by instancing, any card
DLSS; DLSS-NR from the player’s DLL
A larger recommended size, so LMU makes eye targets with room beside each eye for
its focus view. The graphics card checked once: NVIDIA RTX 20 series and newer use
NVIDIA’s multi-view rendering, any other Direct3D 11.3 card Sim-QVFR’s own
Every vertex shader gets twins that draw a second view: NVIDIA’s (through NVAPI) and
the instanced one; input layouts with per-instance data get one with doubled step
rates. Pixel shaders known by checksum: YEBIS’s copy and composite, the final blit;
car paint and the light buffers tagged for night cars; mip-bias twins for texture
The FOV crop taken off each eye before LMU sees it. Eye tracking (or the head)
places each eye’s focus box: a dead-zone against tracker noise, both boxes aimed at
the depth you look at (LMU’s scene depth at the box centre, read without a stall),
its shape and size. With DLSS or FSR the FOV moves by this frame’s sub-pixel jitter
(Halton 2, 3), and the eye poses are kept for the motion vectors.
The pass tracker finds LMU’s two eye passes by their target binds. Live resolution:
the eye’s viewports and scissors cut to the periphery’s size inside LMU’s target,
and a second viewport beside it for the focus view (smaller under DLSS super
resolution). One eye off: that eye’s scene draws are skipped.
What lies outside the focus shape is drawn into the focus view’s depth first, so
LMU’s scene skips those pixels (early depth), with a margin for what DLSS and
Every draw with a depth target runs its twin: NVIDIA’s multi-view rasterises it into
both viewports, or Sim-QVFR’s draws twice the instances, odd ones into the focus
view. The focus view’s clip space is the eye’s remapped (cb13). The lens mask is
drawn in both; LMU’s sun-shadow command lists go through the same detours; DrawAuto
and indirect draws stay eye only.
Overlay badge: MVR, SMVR or Fallback
Each car part’s world matrix read from the per-draw buffer as LMU writes it, this
frame and last: the other cars’ motion vectors. For night cars, the floodlights and
headlights LMU hands each draw are copied at Unmap, and car parts also write a slot
target: the part, the game’s normals, its baked occlusion and bent normals.
Before the first transparent draw that writes depth (the car’s glass), the depth is
copied for DLSS, so its vectors see what lies behind the windscreen.
One full-screen pass over each eye and its focus view relights every car pixel
before the post: ambient occlusion, lacquer highlights per floodlight, paint detail,
floodlight and ground shadows, reflections only where both eyes see them,
headlights, optional night vision; a fill scale tames LMU’s flat light. Quality Low,
Medium or High; the periphery one tier below the focus.
Per view, on the HDR scene before YEBIS: depth, motion vectors from depth (the
cockpit by the head pose, cars by their matrices), then NGX: DLAA on the eyes, DLAA
or super resolution on the focus views, the result back into the scene. DLSS-NR (the
player’s own NVIDIA DLL) on the focus views, the periphery optional, before or after
DLSS. AMD FSR in DLSS’s place without an RTX card. NR and FSR run on a D3D12 device
of Sim-QVFR’s that shares textures and a fence with LMU’s.
LMU’s YEBIS post runs on the eye as shipped. Right after it, its copy and composite
run once more on the focus view, with the game’s own shaders and constants, the
eye’s glare resampled through the focus box and its exposure: the focus view matches
The game’s final blit replayed for the focus view beside the eye. The driver tags’
viewport cut to the rendered size; the VR UI panel (HUD, menus, MFD) drawn into both
views from a mipmapped copy of its canvas; overlays moved back by the jitter.
LMU copies each eye’s final into its swapchain; Sim-QVFR takes the eye and its focus
view from that image. Frames without the race (main menu, loading) are scaled up to
the native eye size before LMU draws its UI.
The periphery upscaled over each eye with the focus view blended in (feather,
shape); CAS sharpening on the focus only; colour correction over all of it; the
helmet, lit by the frame. Composed at the focus views’ density, or on Pimax and
Varjo handed to the runtime as four quad views. Quad layers on top: the headset
menu, the performance overlay, the clock. One eye off: black in that eye.

reloads it while LMU runs and the frame
The headset menu changes the same settings
in VR; Optimize finds the periphery, focus
density and box that fit the frame budget.
Moving the CPU: LMU’s main thread on a core
The overlay: frame rate and pacing, CPU and
GPU against the budget, GPU time by LMU,
Sim-QVFR and the rest, the busiest thread,
VRAM, eye tracking, the multi-view badge and
the night cars’ cost. The log: the passes’
CPU and GPU costs every 900 frames, the
instancing takes over. No focus views for a
while: the eyes at full resolution, tried
again with a growing wait. Another LMU
build: the values from OpenXR and the draws’
constants instead of the reads. If nothing

svg.text: Grey arrows are calls LMU makes anyway; the dashed one is Sim-QVFR reading values in LMU’s data. No arrow points into LMU’s code.
Most settings change live from the launcher or the headset menu; the shader twins for night cars and texture sharpening are made at launch.
Details: LMU-MVR-ARCHITECTURE.svg (NVIDIA’s multi-view), LMU-NEUTRAL-MVR-ARCHITECTURE.svg (Sim-QVFR’s own), LMU-DLSS-ARCHITECTURE.svg (DLSS, FSR).
From src/games/lmu/, src/engine/, src/quad/ and src/layer/ on development (e15d92b, 2026-11-19).
